preconditions.description: The number of bases n and the number of remaining bases k must satisfy 2 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 500,000.
Each of the n lines after the first contains exactly two integers representing coordinates.

preconditions.expression: all(-10**9 <= int(x) <= 10**9 and -10**9 <= int(y) <= 10**9 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x, y in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: Each coordinate x and y must satisfy -10^9 ≤ x, y ≤ 10^9.

preconditions.expression: any('0 0' in line for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: One of the bases must be at the origin (0, 0).

preconditions.expression: len({tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]}) == n
preconditions.description: No two bases have identical coordinates.

postconditions.description: The output is the maximal possible sum of distances between all pairs of k remaining bases, with an absolute or relative error less than 10^-6.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= x <= 10**9 and 0 <= y <= 10**9 for x, y in coordinates)
postconditions.description: The coordinates of the selected k bases are valid (no negative values in the output context, but this is a placeholder for the actual logic).
